description: This file is the implementation of the Error module in Perl, providing object-oriented error and exception handling, including classes such as Error and Error::Simple, along with procedural interfaces like try, catch, finally, and associated error management functions.

classes.name: Error
classes.description: Base class for error objects supporting properties like package, file, line, text, and methods for error management, stringification, and stack trace information.

classes.name: Error::Simple
classes.description: Subclass of Error representing simple error messages with optional value and location info.

classes.name: Error::subs
classes.description: Provides implementation of exception handling syntax including try, catch, finally, except, otherwise constructs.

classes.name: Error::WarnDie
classes.description: Provides warning and die signal handlers that generate stack traces and manage error output.

methods.name: new
methods.description: Constructs a new Error object, capturing package, file, line, and optional text and object.

methods.name: throw
methods.description: Throws the error object, causing program control to transfer to a handler or die.

methods.name: with
methods.description: Creates a new Error object with the provided attributes, for syntactic sugar.

methods.name: record
methods.description: Creates and returns an Error object without throwing it.

methods.name: stacktrace
methods.description: Returns detailed stack trace if debugging is enabled.

methods.name: associate
methods.description: Associates an Error with an object for propagation of errors.

methods.name: object
methods.description: Returns the object associated with the error, if any.

methods.name: file
methods.description: Returns the filename where the error was created.

methods.name: line
methods.description: Returns the line number where the error was created.

methods.name: stringify
methods.description: Stringification method returning the error text.

methods.name: value
methods.description: Returns the associated value of the error.
